questions.question: On the initial failing turn, what does JsonScaffold.step do in this toy repository?
options: It edits the first failing file and returns a JSON edit action
It rewrites every file in one Python snippet
It runs no tests before editing
It changes the model's test expectations
questions.explanation: step runs the deterministic tests, applies the first available per-path FIXES entry, and returns a JSON edit action naming the path.

questions.question: What does CodeActScaffold.worst_touched measure for the three-bug fixture?
options: The number of test assertions
The largest number of files one snippet touched, which is 3
The number of turns used by JSON
The number of files in the initial repository
questions.explanation: The first CodeAct edit fixes app.py, util.py, and cli.py in one snippet, so worst_touched becomes 3.

questions.question: What are the reported turn counts when both scaffolds use their default max_turns?
options: JSON uses 2 and CodeAct uses 4
Both use 3
JSON uses 4 and CodeAct uses 2
JSON uses 10 and CodeAct uses 10
questions.explanation: JSON fixes one failing path per turn and then needs a done turn (4 total); CodeAct fixes all three at once and then needs done (2 total).

questions.question: Why is the comparison meaningful even though both scaffolds use the same FIXES table?
options: The tests are intentionally different for each scaffold
CodeAct never runs tests
The JSON scaffold has no blast radius
The stub model and fixture are shared, so turn and action-shape differences come from the scaffold
questions.explanation: Both paths run the same deterministic run_tests and _apply_fix logic; the orchestration changes how many files an action can touch.

questions.question: What trade-off does the demo attach to CodeAct's shorter run?
options: A single snippet can touch more files, so sandbox isolation must control its larger blast radius
It cannot pass the same tests
It always needs more turns than JSON
It removes the repository's test suite
questions.explanation: CodeAct compresses three edits into one action (two turns total), but that action has an observed blast radius of three files.

questions.question: Which initial source change fixes the app.py fixture?
options: Replace VERSION v0.0 with v1.0
Replace return a - b with return a + b
Replace s.upper() with s.lower()
Add a fourth test to TESTS
questions.explanation: The first test expects add(2, 3) == 5, so the app.py rule changes the subtraction expression to addition.
